channel.title: Acme: Daily Reading List
channel.description: Noteworthy articles from across the web.

item.title: St. Augustine’s Ximenez-Fatio House wins $750,000 preservation grant
item.description: The 1798 coquina house will receive a three-year National Park Service grant for interior and exterior preservation. The museum interprets Spanish, Minorcan, colonial and 228 years of African American history, with archaeology reaching back to pre-Columbian times.

item.title: The XML-RPC spec’s timezone answer is still a warning for implementors
item.description: Dave Winer’s compact XML-RPC specification leaves dateTime.iso8601 timezone assumptions to each server’s documentation. That small ambiguity explains why compatible implementations still need an explicit convention rather than silently treating timestamps as local time or UTC.

item.title: Public Domain Day guide maps the tangled rights inside classic characters
item.description: Duke’s 2026 guide separates expired copyrights, unrenewed works, later protected additions and trademarks. Its Betty Boop and Mickey examples show why a character can be free to reuse in one form while later plots, dialogue or designs remain protected.
item.source: Center for the Study of the Public Domain

item.title: FeedLand's public package separates the server API from its database layer
item.description: The FeedLand package is useful reading for a compatible PHP port because it exposes the server application, documents a separate database package and carries the project's GPL-2.0 license. The repository offers a concrete map of the upstream contracts an independent implementation must preserve.

item.title: An rssCloud implementor explains why thin pings keep the server simple
item.description: Andrew Shell's implementation notes contrast rssCloud's URL-only notification with WebSub's content-bearing ping. The distinction is practical for a FeedLand-compatible subscriber: the cloud stays lightweight, while feed fetching, parsing and deduplication remain the client's responsibility.

item.title: Jacksonville's road-first growth explains its long transit struggle
item.description: Historian Alan Bliss traces how flat land, suburban expansion, cheap parking and an expressway authority built around road engineering marginalized Jacksonville transit. The essay connects those inherited assumptions to today's JTA financial crisis and the city's renewed debate over a future system.

item.title: ServiceNow documents how REST endpoint ACLs layer over table access
item.description: ServiceNow's current guidance says Scripted REST requests already respect table ACLs, while a REST_Endpoint ACL can add another gate to the entire API. A caller must satisfy at least one selected endpoint ACL, and individual resources can override the API-wide setting.

item.title: Library of Congress traces the Black creators behind Golden Legacy
item.description: The Library of Congress recounts how Bertram A. Fitzgerald published 16 issues of Golden Legacy from 1966 to 1976. Fitzgerald wrote and edited early issues, then hired Black creators including Tom Feelings, Joan Bacchus Maynard and Ezra Jackson to dramatize Black history.

item.title: YouTube's faster Content ID appeal path carries a higher risk
item.description: YouTube shortened the claimant response window for Content ID appeals from 30 days to seven and added a route that can skip the initial dispute for blocked videos. The tradeoff matters: if the claimant rejects an appeal, the next step can be a formal removal request and a channel strike.

item.title: Composer 2.11 release candidate adds safer package policies
item.description: Composer 2.11 RC1 adds a cooldown policy for withholding newly released packages, direct-dependency audits, stricter PSR autoloading and improved dependency-resolution performance. The maintainers are asking PHP developers to test the preview and report regressions before the final release.

item.title: A full-text RSS dispute tests the boundary between syndication and republication
item.description: An independent publisher documents how RSS Amplifier republished 19 complete articles and offered substitute feeds without permission. The case is a useful reminder that making full-text RSS available to readers does not surrender copyright or authorize another site to mirror an archive.

item.title: Mark Evanier remembers pioneering comics artist Fred Guardineer
item.description: Mark Evanier's obituary traces Fred Guardineer from pulp illustration and the Harry Chesler shop to Zatara, Speed Saunders and striking Golden Age covers. Guardineer later drew for publishers including Fawcett before leaving comics during the industry's mid-1950s slump.

item.title: A 2026 public-domain guide separates free characters from later versions
item.description: Aaron Moss surveys works from 1930 and sound recordings from 1925 that became free to use in the United States, including early Betty Boop, Blondie and Mickey Mouse comic strips. The guide also explains why only the traits present in those newly open versions are safe territory.

item.title: Florida HOA law does not guarantee political-yard-sign rights
item.description: This focused guide distinguishes Florida's statutory protection for specified flags from political signs, which the HOA statute does not separately protect. Whether a campaign sign is allowed usually turns on the recorded declaration and association rules, with public rights-of-way governed separately.

item.title: A digital exhibit puts Revolutionary-era St. Augustine online
item.description: The Governor's House Library digitized every panel of Florida at War, its exhibit on St. Augustine during the American Revolution. The online version makes maps, primary-source research and the city's role as a British military and refugee center available beyond the museum.
